content.comment_body: I'm having an issue where the text display doesn't show the enabled text blocks as expected when switching messages. For instance, in my setup, pressing F4 on the display enables the first message block. Pressing ESC + C> activates the next text message and disables the previous one, but the buttons often require multiple presses and aren't very reliable—though everything works fine on the actual module. Most of the time, the text display just reverts to showing the time and date screen, which is normally accessed with the Cv button, and won't return to the selected message. On the module, the correct message is shown and I can navigate screens without issues. Oddly, pressing F3 in my program enables M27 for the second message in the text block, which works perfectly—messages appear correctly on both the display and module, and navigation is smooth. Pressing F3 again disables M27, but then the display stays stuck on time and date. Maybe this is an issue with the display's firmware?
Hello, For questions like this, it's best to share the part number, firmware version of your module, and the text display's firmware version.

I can't recall the exact details right now, but it's a brand new [article_no] module—I'm using [product_name] V7.1.5 for programming. The text display is also new. From memory, its firmware is something like V7.0.3.
Hello, Even though both the module and the display are new out of the box, there may still be a firmware version conflict causing your issue. Check the related discussion thread for similar problems.
I think the link you provided redirects to this same thread.
It works now. Can you tell me what the latest firmware versions are?
Hi, Why do you always ask about the firmware version? Firmware can't be changed in these units. Hope this clarifies things.
I know you can't update the firmware, but I'm asking to check if I have the newest text display. Then I can figure out if it's a firmware issue or something else.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing inconsistent behavior when switching text messages via the display—while the main module shows the correct enabled messages, the text display often defaults back to the time and date screen. This inconsistency, especially during navigation, suggests possible firmware limitations or incompatibilities with the text display handling enabled message blocks.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the text display to reliably show the selected message, just like the main module does, and not revert unexpectedly to the time and date screen during message switching.
